metadata.scope: Production UI, controllers, shared database, foreground collectors/tasks and notification response/timing boundaries. Inventory records explicit scenarios and limitations, not exhaustive proof of every possible product interaction.

harness_limits: ForegroundUiHarness substitutes an in-memory notification controller. It records calls to show/schedule/cancel but does not prove native OS rendering, delivery, sound, permission behavior, or background delivery timing.
The native controller contract test mocks the Flutter local-notifications MethodChannel; it validates serialized plugin calls but does not invoke platform OS notification APIs.

UI scenarios share independent UI and foreground database clients backed by one in-memory Drift database; they do not cover persistent on-device database recovery unless a separate recovery test is listed.

scenarios.feature: Finished-eating reminder timing
scenarios.trigger: MealStartedEatingEvent; mutable clock and WorkflowScheduler ticks; snooze and agree responses use serialized notification wire through ExternalEventHandler.
scenarios.expectedUI: No notification or completion widget is mounted; fake OS port and persisted completion handoff are observed.
scenarios.expectedDB: Meal transitions from eating to eaten in both clients with exactly one eaten history entry.
scenarios.expectedFG: FinishedEatingNotificationEvent is absent before five minutes, shown once at five minutes, shown again five minutes after snooze, and not repeated after agree. Agree cancels the active finished-eating notification and schedules one summary reminder for two minutes later.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Foreground task to timed fake NotificationsController; serialized snooze and agree go through ExternalEventHandler.

scenarios.feature: Activity confirmation timing and pre-deadline deletion
scenarios.trigger: ActivityScheduleTask receives a tick at and just before each occurrence actionAt; user deletes the later occurrence from ActivityUpcomingList.
scenarios.expectedUI: Production upcoming-activity list delete action is used.
scenarios.expectedDB: Deleted occurrence is asserted to have status deleted.
scenarios.expectedFG: No activity confirmation before the retained occurrence actionAt; exactly one ActivityScheduleNotificationEvent at that boundary with its occurrence ID; deleted occurrence produces no later prompt.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Foreground task to fake NotificationsController; actual UI deletion before the notification deadline.

scenarios.feature: Delete an occurrence after its confirmation is already shown
scenarios.trigger: Activity confirmation is shown at actionAt, then the occurrence is deleted from ActivityUpcomingList.
scenarios.expectedUI: Production upcoming-activity list delete action is used.
scenarios.expectedDB: Deletion action updates the occurrence; the skipped body expects the notification key to no longer be active.
scenarios.expectedFG: Already shown ActivityScheduleNotificationEvent should be cancelled and not remain active.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Foreground task to fake NotificationsController; assertion checks active notification identity.
scenarios.previousKnownDefect: Skipped (skip: true): ActivityScheduleService delete/remove currently does not cancel an already shown activity confirmation notification.
scenarios.verification: Enabled and passed in the complete regression after production repair.

scenarios.feature: Serialized finished-eating response for a late meal
scenarios.trigger: ExternalEventHandler receives the serialized Agree action for FinishedEatingNotificationEvent.
scenarios.expectedUI: No completion screen is mounted; the foreground-to-UI router receives task_open_meal_completion for the meal.
scenarios.expectedDB: Meal remains eating in both clients and status history is unchanged while completion handling is pending.
scenarios.expectedFG: Pending meal completion request contains the meal ID; serialized Agree does not mutate meal status directly.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Serialized notification response wire to ExternalEventHandler.
scenarios.knownskip/gap: The test verifies a navigation handoff and pending request, not that the completion screen actually opens.

scenarios.feature: Finished-eating snooze and dismiss response
scenarios.trigger: ExternalEventHandler receives serialized snooze and empty actions for the target meal notification.
scenarios.expectedUI: No notification or completion screen rendering assertion.
scenarios.expectedDB: Target meal, unrelated meal, and their status history remain unchanged.
scenarios.expectedFG: Foreground-to-UI router receives no messages for snooze or empty; this case does not test the task's snooze timer.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Serialized snooze and empty response wire actions.

scenarios.feature: Meal summary reminder Agree
scenarios.trigger: ExternalEventHandler receives serialized Agree twice for a MealSummaryReminderNotificationEvent.
scenarios.expectedUI: MealListToday refreshes; after summary Agree the ready meal disappears from the list.
scenarios.expectedDB: Meal is summarized in both clients; consumed amount and one consumed snapshot are asserted; unrelated planned meal remains unchanged.
scenarios.expectedFG: No notification delivery or schedule-time assertion.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Serialized notification response wire through ExternalEventHandler.

scenarios.feature: Notification response identity guards
scenarios.trigger: Finished-eating Agree actions use an unknown meal ID and a deleted meal ID.
scenarios.expectedUI: No rendered UI assertion.
scenarios.expectedDB: Valid meal and history remain unchanged.
scenarios.expectedFG: No navigation handoff; pending completion request set remains empty.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Serialized response wire; unknown and deleted entity identities.

scenarios.feature: Activity schedule response Agree and skip
scenarios.trigger: ExternalEventHandler receives serialized Agree and skip actions for separate activity occurrence IDs.
scenarios.expectedUI: ActivityUpcomingList is mounted and refreshes; planned and skipped labels are asserted.
scenarios.expectedDB: Agreed occurrence becomes planned and has a linked activity log; skipped occurrence becomes skipped; unrelated occurrence remains pending.
scenarios.expectedFG: Response event updates the relevant occurrence through production schedule service; no notification timing or active-notification cancellation assertion.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Serialized activity-schedule notification response wire.

scenarios.feature: Serialized response action routing for Eat Now, meal suggestion, AAPS carbs request, and finished activity
scenarios.trigger: ExternalEventHandler receives production notification payloads converted to notification-response wire actions; typed EventInbox subscriptions are opened before dispatch.
scenarios.expectedUI: No visible UI is asserted; route integration is tested against the real ExternalEventHandler and shared foreground runtime.
scenarios.expectedDB: Finished-activity response is asserted not to mutate its activity log because repository search found no production consumer for ActivityFinishedResponseEvent.
scenarios.expectedFG: Eat Now and meal-suggestion responses emit the expected typed events; AAPS carbs Agree emits the matching acknowledgement; AAPS empty action sends task_open_low_treatment; activity-finished Agree emits its typed response event.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Actual notification.toPayload() response data is wrapped in serialized ExternalEventHandler wire; no native OS callback is invoked here.
scenarios.knownskip/gap: ActivityFinishedNotificationEvent has no production emitter, and ActivityFinishedResponseEvent has no production consumer. The test documents a dormant event type, not a live user flow.

scenarios.feature: Native callback forwarding
scenarios.trigger: Flutter notification callback receives a selected action for a finished-eating notification and forwards serialized data through the recording platform.
scenarios.expectedUI: No rendered UI assertion.
scenarios.expectedDB: Meal remains eating after callback dispatch.
scenarios.expectedFG: Exactly one platform message and the task_open_meal_completion handoff are recorded; pending request contains the meal ID. No native notification presentation/delivery is asserted.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Flutter callback adapter to recording platform to ExternalEventHandler.
scenarios.knownskip/gap: Only the finished-eating action is exercised through the native callback adapter.

scenarios.feature: Local notification controller summary-reminder schedule contract
scenarios.trigger: LocalNotificationsController shows and schedules summary reminders for two meal IDs with a two-minute delay, then cancels one ID.
scenarios.expectedUI: No widgets or OS notifications are rendered.
scenarios.expectedDB: No database access or mutation.
scenarios.expectedFG: Actual FlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin Android MethodChannel calls carry a zoned schedule between real before/after time-plus-delay bounds, Europe/Warsaw wall time, exactAllowWhileIdle, and the summary response payload with meal ID. Show/schedule/cancel share stable per-entity IDs; cancelling one leaves the other pending.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: LocalNotificationsController to FlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin MethodChannel; all platform reads/writes are mocked and recorded.
scenarios.knownskip/gap: Does not validate OS alarm delivery, exact-alarm permission, rendering, or background execution.

scenarios.feature: Activity scheduled confirmation task boundaries
scenarios.trigger: WorkflowScheduler ticks the activity schedule task through pending, action, restart, and confirmation windows.
scenarios.expectedUI: No UI widgets are mounted.
scenarios.expectedDB: Confirm response creates an activity log; restart preserves occurrence state; previous-evening confirmation reserves the session.
scenarios.expectedFG: Task tests assert notification types and counts around configured action times; they do not use wall-clock timed history.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: ActivityScheduleTask to fake NotificationsController; direct typed task responses.

scenarios.feature: Meal monitor notification timing and cleanup
scenarios.trigger: FakeAsync advances meal monitor task through finished-eating reminder, snooze, agree, and interruption paths.
scenarios.expectedUI: No UI widgets are mounted.
scenarios.expectedDB: Assertions vary by task case; completion and interruption cases cover status/update behavior.
scenarios.expectedFG: Reminder timing, notification type, entity ID, scheduling, and cancellation are asserted in selected cases.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: MealMonitorTask to fake NotificationsController; direct typed task responses.
scenarios.knownskip/gap: Task-level evidence does not prove native OS rendering or delivery.

scenarios.feature: Activity notification cleanup on session finish
scenarios.trigger: Activity monitor finishes a session that owns activity-scoped notifications.
scenarios.expectedUI: No UI widgets are mounted.
scenarios.expectedDB: Existing session and occurrence rows are used to resolve the finished activity scope.
scenarios.expectedFG: Scoped activity notifications are cancelled while other activity and meal notifications remain active.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Activity monitor task/executor to fake NotificationsController.

scenarios.feature: Create meal through the production review flow
scenarios.trigger: User advances through meal timing/review, selects a category, then saves; companion cases cancel before final save or tap save twice rapidly.
scenarios.expectedUI: Production AddMealPage review flow is used; category and review controls are exercised.
scenarios.expectedDB: Saved meal and ingredient persist in both DB clients; rapid taps create one row. Cancel before save leaves both meal tables empty.
scenarios.expectedFG: Saved planned meal is published to meal monitoring; cancel leaves monitoring idle.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification assertion; foreground monitor state is observed.

scenarios.feature: Start a planned meal from manual decision UI
scenarios.trigger: User selects food-first, insulin-and-wait, or insulin-and-food-now decision and starts the meal; companion cancels a manual decision.
scenarios.expectedUI: Production meal status dialog, manual decision form, and next action are exercised.
scenarios.expectedDB: Meal status becomes eating-then-bolus or waiting-for-bolus; plannedAt remains fixed and meal advisor result records manual choice and initial wait. Cancel leaves status planned.
scenarios.expectedFG: Monitoring phase and meal ID match the persisted state; foreground monitor observes the selected transition.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification delivery assertion; test launcher and UI actions are used.

scenarios.feature: Planned meal display, skip, deletion, and replacement monitoring
scenarios.trigger: Production meal list and status dialog actions display, skip, or delete planned meals; duplicate skip confirmation is tapped twice; another active meal blocks starting a planned meal.
scenarios.expectedUI: MealListToday and MealStatusDialog are exercised; confirmed skip updates the UI, cancelled skip leaves it open and unchanged.
scenarios.expectedDB: Skip writes one skipped history row in each client; duplicate confirmation persists once. Delete removes meal. Active-meal guard leaves selected planned and active rows unchanged.
scenarios.expectedFG: Foreground status follows the planned meal, stops after skip/delete, and selects replacement meal after deleting the first of two.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification delivery assertions.
scenarios.previousKnownDefect: The last-planned-meal deletion scenario is skipped: NextMealCollector does not publish removal of the last planned meal.
scenarios.verification: Enabled and passed in the complete regression after production repair.

scenarios.feature: Meal completion editor and monitor handoff
scenarios.trigger: User saves planned or adjusted consumed amount from MealCompletionView; companion cases cancel, or complete in eat-then-bolus flow.
scenarios.expectedUI: Production completion view and amount selector are exercised; saved or cancelled completion view closes/continues as expected.
scenarios.expectedDB: Consumed amount is stored in both DB clients; adjusted values update consumed macro totals; eat-then-bolus persists waiting-for-bolus, status history, and consumed snapshot. Cancel preserves eating state and amount.
scenarios.expectedFG: After summary, meal monitor is idle; when waiting for bolus, monitor remains in WaitForBolusExecutor.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification timing or native notification delivery assertion.

scenarios.feature: Interrupt an active meal through production UI
scenarios.trigger: User cancels interruption, confirms stop-tracking, encounters a stale confirmation after a terminal status, or cold-restores with multiple meals.
scenarios.expectedUI: MealListToday and active progress card show or remove the active meal as the status changes.
scenarios.expectedDB: Cancel preserves both clients, status history, and snapshots. Confirm writes one interrupted status in both clients and no snapshots. Stale confirmation does not overwrite eaten status.
scenarios.expectedFG: Cancel preserves active monitor; confirmed interruption returns monitor to idle; cold restore selects eating meal and keeps it aligned with the active card.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification timing assertion; interruption is an in-app UI action.

scenarios.feature: Add-on meal amount editor
scenarios.trigger: User cancels add-on choices/editor or confirms a larger portion from eating and bolused-eating states.
scenarios.expectedUI: Production add-on choice and MealAddOnEditor are exercised; cancellation closes editor without committing.
scenarios.expectedDB: Cancel preserves status and consumed amounts. Confirm scales ingredient consumption once in both clients and persists add-on bolus context with covered/requested carbs.
scenarios.expectedFG: Confirmed add-on sets eating-extra data and waiting-for-bolus phase for the meal; cancelled add-on preserves current monitoring status.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification boundary assertion.

scenarios.feature: Activity dashboard and upcoming activity UI
scenarios.trigger: Activity starts/auto-ends, user cancels a planned activity, edits duration/details, or moves an upcoming occurrence; duplicate start while active has a skipped regression case.
scenarios.expectedUI: DashboardStatusCard, completed summary card, ActivityPage, picker sheet, and ActivityUpcomingList production actions are exercised.
scenarios.expectedDB: Finish closes log; cancel planned action removes planned log; edit cancel leaves DB unchanged; upcoming move creates skipped old and pending moved occurrence rows in both DB clients.
scenarios.expectedFG: Active/preparing status and log IDs match selected activity; auto-end publishes summary-ready state; moved occurrence no longer retains old prompt identity.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Upcoming move case uses fake notification controller to assert the old prompt key is no longer active; no native OS delivery assertion.
scenarios.previousKnownDefect: Two cases are skipped: starting another activity while one is active can insert a second open log; running monitor snapshots its default duration and ignores later duration edits.
scenarios.verification: Enabled and passed in the complete regression after production repair.

scenarios.feature: Glucose foreground and dashboard synchronization
scenarios.trigger: Local glucose handler receives fresh, wrong-source, duplicate, expired, or late readings; returning UI requests cache synchronization.
scenarios.expectedUI: Dashboard glucose view shows accepted value, returns to unknown after expiry, and displays synchronized history on UI return.
scenarios.expectedDB: Synced history contains newest-first accepted readings with unique timestamps; late-sample cases do not mutate a database assertion.
scenarios.expectedFG: Foreground value accepts fresh configured source, ignores wrong-source/duplicate values, expires after six minutes, and supplies cache values to UI.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification actions; test observes foreground providers and sync event router.
scenarios.previousKnownDefect: Late 2-minute and 7-minute sample cases are skipped because a delayed old sample may replace or clear the current value.
scenarios.verification: Enabled and passed in the complete regression after production repair.

scenarios.feature: Pump device status dashboard synchronization
scenarios.trigger: Local device status handler receives fresh, wrong-source, invalid-BG, or late pump status.
scenarios.expectedUI: DeviceStatusDashboard displays IOB and COB from accepted sample and preserves current values on rejected samples.
scenarios.expectedDB: No database persistence assertion in these scenarios.
scenarios.expectedFG: Foreground device status provider accepts valid configured-source sample and rejects wrong-source or invalid-BG sample.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification actions; device status adapter and app transport are exercised.
scenarios.previousKnownDefect: Late 2-minute and 7-minute status cases are skipped because old status can roll back or clear the current sample.
scenarios.verification: Enabled and passed in the complete regression after production repair.

scenarios.feature: Data source settings and foreground config synchronization
scenarios.trigger: User changes glucose source and mirror-to-local setting, tries unavailable source, or opens settings at narrow width.
scenarios.expectedUI: DataSourceSettingsSection dropdown and switch are exercised; unavailable sources are absent; narrow-width history dropdown has a skipped no-overflow regression.
scenarios.expectedDB: Shared preference keys persist selected source and mirror setting.
scenarios.expectedFG: Foreground DataSourceConfig reflects persisted source and mirror setting after app-event transport.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: No notification actions; app event router is observed.
scenarios.previousKnownDefect: Narrow-layout no-overflow scenario is skipped due to a known HistorySource dropdown overflow.
scenarios.verification: Enabled and passed in the complete regression after production repair.

scenarios.feature: Notification completion navigation and recovery
scenarios.trigger: Late finished-eating Agree with UI present or absent; actual TaskEventHandler and deferred UI recovery.
scenarios.expectedUI: Real MealCompletionEntry opens for the requested meal, once. Cancel closes it; a concurrent recovery must not reopen the dismissed sheet.
scenarios.expectedDB: Eating status, consumed amount and status history remain unchanged until explicit completion; pending navigation intent is acknowledged after cancel.
scenarios.expectedFG: Serialized ExternalEventHandler response persists and forwards the completion intent; UI consumes the production task payload.
scenarios.notificationboundary/actions: Serialized response -> foreground handler -> task bridge -> TaskEventHandler -> production completion sheet.
scenarios.verification: Enabled and passed in the complete regression after production repair.
scenarios.previousKnownDefect: Concurrent recovery case is skipped: a recovery completing after cancellation reopens the acknowledged sheet. Ordinary recovery and direct navigation controls remain enabled.

approvedExpectationChanges.scope: Two scenarios: protein 15 -> 14; carbs/net carbs 2 -> 1, plus the sum-rounding scenario title. User approved explicitly.
Only the missing-conversion scenario: assert unavailable conversion and no manufactured gram amounts instead of a one-gram fallback. User approved explicitly.

repairVerification.otherExistingExpectations: Preserved. New integration fixtures received complete notification-port mocks and bounded semantic frame/I/O waits.
additionalProtection: Backup import preserves known and unknown conversion metadata transactionally, including rollback.
Copy, preview, summary, similarity and LLM paths share recorded quantities and historical source availability.
Optional snapshot-history failure preserves independently available chart and timeline context.
Collector disposal cancels timers and releases waits without relying on runtime shutdown.
repairVerification.legacyPolicy: Do not fill absent historical conversions from current mappings or claim an exact calculation time from ambiguous metadata. Preserve authoritative saved aggregates and expose unavailable supporting facts.
repairVerification.coverageMeaning: All 175 concrete use-case/controller classes and both function use cases executed. 333 executable lines remain uncovered; execution coverage is not proof of every possible business scenario.
